Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — we need a plan for the Nov product launch coinciding with end-of-quarter promos + a smaller Black Friday test. Goal: avoid cold-start thundering herd in eu-west and ap-south, keep p99 below 250ms for conversational routes.
Maria Gonzalez: timeline? when do we start pre-warm?
Alex Chen: pre-warm window proposal: start 36h before launch traffic ramp, full pool warmed 12h before. Pre-warm = keep KV cache hot + run synthetic steady QPS to keep pods in steady-state.
Jon Peterson: rough numbers: baseline steady GPUs for that route = 80 vGPUs across us-east + 20 in eu-west. Peak surge multiplier expected ~3x for first 6 hours. So add ~160 vGPU-hours/hr headroom at peak, ~960 vGPU-hours over 6h.
Sara Li: if we do 36h pre-warm that's extra cost. can we mitigate with staggered warming and routing policies? e.g., warm 50% earlier, then spin up the rest closer to ramp.
Maria Gonzalez: agree. staggered warm + traffic shaping via smart routing. route low-priority traffic to quantized model variants during warmup.
Alex Chen: cost estimate quick calc: extra reserved GPU-hours for 36h prewarm (averaged): 40 GPUs * 36h = 1440 GPU-hours. Add 960 GPU-hours for the 6h peak buffer = ~2400 GPU-hours. At committed rate that's a material bump.
Jon Peterson: suggestion: use Dedicated burst pool for first 2h of launch only, then fall back to reserved. That reduces long prewarm cost. Also enable tiny-canary to validate model state.
Maria Gonzalez: are there region constraints? APAC has limited Dedicated capacity for our instance type; we may need to fall back to a smaller instance or shift requests to us-central with higher egress.
Sara Li: network egress costs and latency tradeoff — shifting to us-central adds ~40ms median for APAC users, but holds latency SLOs for text-generation (p95 still okay). Need sign-off if we shift traffic cross-region.
Alex Chen: proposal finalized:
- Prewarm plan: staggered prewarm over 36h (25% / 50% / 25% steps)
- Canary: start tiny traffic at T-12h, validate KV hitrates and decode perf
- Burst: enable Dedicated burst pool for T+0-2h (auto-release)+ fallback routing to quantized model variants at T+2h if pressure persists
- Region hedge: route APAC to eu-west only if us-east capacity exhausted; fallback to us-central with egress tag and cost alarm
- Cost guardrails: set budget alarm at +15% expected committed usage, autoscaling throttles after threshold

Infra-bot: Created capacity-playbook ticket #CAP-2025 and scheduled a prewarm job at 1742460000 (T-36h)
Jon Peterson: We'll run a dry-run with the loadsim script tomorrow. command for load generator:
```
./loadsim --profile=nov-launch --qps=4500 --duration=2h --seq-dist=short
```
Sara Li: I'll own routing policy changes and knobs: cooldown=30s -> set to 20s for launch, batcher window tighten from 80ms -> 40ms for lower tail latency.
Maria Gonzalez: I'll coordinate with finance for temporary committed capacity and get APAC approval for cross-region egress.
Alex Chen: Action items: Jon run dry-run + upload logs to /ops/capacity/nov-launch/, Maria confirm budget/commit by EOD tomorrow, Sara implement routing changes in staging and post canary metrics.
Jon Peterson: ack. starting sims at 09:00 PT tomorrow. Will paste results here. :rocket:
Sara Li: added a data point — turn on prefix caching for common prompts. cheap wins for token cost.
Alex Chen: perfect. if any infra anomalies during dry-run, tag me and @infra-oncall.
Maria Gonzalez: noted. thanks team.
Infra-bot: Reminder: cap-playbook ticket #CAP-2025 assigned to Alex, Maria, Jon, Sara. Due: 1742470800 (T-20h)
